# 07/10/2026 10:11 — Your Future AI Job Map

Partner, I think the market **is still discovering the job titles**, but the underlying work is becoming much clearer.

The strongest signal I see in 2026 is not “everyone becomes a prompt engineer.” It is:

> **AI executes more. Humans who can define, architect, connect, verify, debug and own the outcome become more valuable.**

LinkedIn says **1.3 million AI-enabled jobs** have emerged globally in two years, explicitly highlighting **AI Engineer and Forward-Deployed Engineer**. UK Head-of-AI roles are also up 30% year-on-year. citeturn0search7 Microsoft describes the same shift differently: as agents take more execution, the premium moves toward **judgment, clarity of intent, quality control and designing how humans and agents work together**. citeturn0search6

That is unusually close to what you have already started doing with TalkProof — but there is an important distinction between **doing it with AI** and being able to **technically own what AI built**.

## The 6 job families I expect to matter

These aren't necessarily the exact titles employers will use in 2028–2030. Think of them as **capability clusters**.

| Future job family | What the person actually owns | Importance | Your estimated gap today |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| **1. Applied / Agentic AI Engineer** | RAG, agents, MCP/tools, APIs, evals, production AI | 🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥 | **30–40%** |
| **2. AI Systems / Solutions Architect** | End-to-end AI + data + cloud + security + enterprise integration | 🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥 | **25–35%** |
| **3. Forward-Deployed AI Engineer** | Take messy customer/business problem → working production system | 🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥 | **30–40%** |
| **4. AI Technical Product Engineer / Owner** | Decide what to build, specify it, orchestrate AI builders, verify outcomes | 🔥🔥🔥🔥 | **20–30%** |
| **5. AI Reliability / Evaluation Engineer** | Determine whether AI systems actually work safely and consistently | 🔥🔥🔥🔥 | **30–40%** |
| **6. AI Platform / LLMOps Engineer** | Deployment, observability, security, scaling, cost, reliability | 🔥🔥🔥🔥 | **45–55%** |

These estimates are **my assessment, not measured test results**. I would change them after testing you against real TalkProof code.

The direction is supported by the broader market too: WEF says AI/big data are the fastest-growing skills, followed by cybersecurity and technological literacy, while analytical thinking, leadership, resilience and lifelong learning remain important. citeturn0search1 The ILO's August 2026 report similarly says AI adoption is increasing demand for higher-order cognitive skills alongside digital and AI capability. citeturn0search5

---

# If the hiring decision were completely mine

I **would recruit you**, but I would be careful about the role.

I would **not currently hire you as a pure Senior Software Engineer** whose value proposition is:

> “Give Senthil a blank laptop, remove AI, and he'll personally implement a complex production system faster than other senior programmers.”

I don't have evidence for that.

I also wouldn't yet hire you as a **Senior AI Platform/LLMOps Engineer**, because production operations, cloud depth, observability, security and independent debugging aren't sufficiently proven.

### I would seriously consider you for:

**AI Systems Builder / Applied AI Engineer moving toward AI Systems Architect.**

Your unusual combination is:

**20+ years data/enterprise context**  
→ SQL/data engineering/business systems  
→ AI-assisted product construction  
→ requirements/architecture  
→ agent/RAG/MCP thinking  
→ Git/evidence/testing/review discipline  
→ business-process understanding  
→ increasingly, technical ownership.

The missing piece is not another 100 AI concepts.

It is:

> **Can Senthil independently explain, predict, challenge, diagnose and decide when the AI-built system fails?**

That is the gap I would attack.

Microsoft's 2026 research is particularly relevant here. Its most advanced “Frontier Professionals” use agents for multi-step work and multi-agent systems, but deliberately retain human judgment and quality control rather than outsourcing their thinking. citeturn0search6

---

# Your skill map

I would score you approximately like this **today**, pending practical testing:

| Capability | Current | Hiring target | Gap |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Enterprise/data engineering | **8.5/10** | 8 | ✅ |
| SQL/data architecture | **9/10** | 8 | ✅ |
| Business → technical problem decomposition | **8.5/10** | 8 | ✅ |
| AI-assisted engineering | **9/10** | 8 | ✅ |
| Requirements/product architecture | **8/10** | 8 | ✅ |
| Agent/RAG/MCP conceptual understanding | **7/10** | 8 | 🟡 |
| Python/backend engineering | **6–7/10** | 8 | 🟡 |
| APIs/distributed-system reasoning | **6.5/10** | 8 | 🟡 |
| AI evaluation/guardrails | **6.5/10** | 8 | 🟡 |
| Security/auth/multi-tenancy | **5–6/10** | 7.5 | 🔴 |
| Azure/cloud architecture | **5.5–6.5/10** | 8 | 🔴 |
| Production debugging | **5–6/10 proven** | 8 | 🔴 |
| Observability/LLMOps | **4.5–5.5/10** | 7.5 | 🔴 |
| React/TypeScript/frontend | **3–4/10** | 6 | 🔴 |
| Independent technical explanation | **?** | 8 | **must test** |

Notice something important.

**React isn't your biggest problem.**

I wouldn't spend three months trying to turn you into a frontend specialist.

Your highest-return gaps are:

**production debugging → backend fundamentals → AI evaluation → security → cloud/operations.**

---

# The job I would train you for

I would **not chase ten future job titles**.

I'd build one profile:

## **Senior Applied AI / Agentic Systems Engineer**

with a trajectory toward:

## **AI Systems Architect / Technical AI Lead**

That profile survives title changes.

The market already points toward it. LinkedIn reports AI-literacy requirements grew 70% year-on-year and describes emerging “new-collar” roles as combining technical fluency with human problem-solving and adaptability. citeturn0search3turn0search7

And this is precisely why your existing data-engineering background matters rather than becoming obsolete.

---

# How you and I close the gap

I would **stop learning primarily through courses**.

TalkProof should become your laboratory.

Every important concept gets taught against something real:

**Teach → locate it in TalkProof → trace execution → break it → diagnose it → repair/decide → explain it without AI.**

For example, take one real inbound call:

`Phone call`

→ carrier/Twilio/Retell  
→ webhook  
→ authentication/signature  
→ tenant resolution  
→ API  
→ database  
→ AI pipeline  
→ RAG/tool call  
→ response  
→ logging  
→ retry  
→ failure handling  
→ observability  
→ cost.

You should eventually be able to stop me anywhere in that chain and explain:

**What happens next? Why? What could fail? How would you know? Where would you look? What would you change?**

That is senior-engineer ownership.

---

# How long?

Assuming roughly **15–20 serious hours/week**, not passive AI chatting:

### Phase 1 — 4 weeks: foundations through TalkProof

Python/FastAPI execution, HTTP/API lifecycle, async, databases/transactions, authentication, dependency injection, queues/webhooks, Git and tests.

You already know pieces. We connect them into one mental model.

**Expected gap: ~35% → ~25%.**

### Phase 2 — 4 weeks: AI engineering depth

RAG end-to-end, embeddings/retrieval/reranking, agent state, MCP/tools, structured output, hallucination/failure modes, evals, guardrails, model routing, context engineering.

But you must **predict/debug**, not merely describe definitions.

**~25% → ~15–20%.**

### Phase 3 — 4 weeks: production engineering

Azure deployment, containers, CI/CD, secrets, identity/RBAC, observability, traces, retries/idempotency, scaling, failure recovery, cost and security.

This is currently the highest-value missing layer.

**~20% → ~10–15%.**

### Phase 4 — 4 weeks: prove ownership

I give you failures without telling you the answer.

“RAG gives the wrong answer.”

“Webhook duplicated a call.”

“Tenant B received tenant A's result.”

“Agent repeatedly invokes the same tool.”

“Latency jumped from 800 ms to 7 seconds.”

“LLM bill increased 4×.”

You investigate.

AI can assist **after you form your diagnosis**, not before.

Then we practise architecture explanation and interviews.

### **My estimate: 12–16 weeks**

Not “master everything in computer science.”

Rather:

> **12–16 weeks to turn your current experience into a defensible Senior Applied/Agentic AI Engineer profile**, provided the practical tests demonstrate the baseline I currently think you have.

For **AI Systems Architect**, I would give it closer to **6–9 months of deliberate production-oriented work**.

For genuine **AI Platform/LLMOps specialist** depth, likely **9–18 months**. I wouldn't make that your primary target.

---

# There is one risk I would take very seriously

Your biggest threat isn't lack of knowledge.

It is becoming **extremely capable at directing AI while your own diagnostic model remains shallower than the system you're directing**.

You've already noticed this issue yourself with TalkProof.

AI can make:

> 20,000 lines  
> 190 endpoints  
> 55 tables  
> thousands of passing tests

appear extremely quickly.

That creates a strange new engineering problem:

**software production speed can exceed human comprehension speed.**

So your training cannot try to match Claude's typing speed.

We need to increase your **comprehension and ownership speed**.

That is why your current TalkProof arrangement — Claude building, ChatGPT independently reviewing/training, you owning the decisions — could actually become an excellent training environment **if we deliberately prevent AI from hiding the engineering from you**. memcite

---

# And I think your age/experience changes the strategy

I wouldn't try to transform you into a 25-year-old programmer competing on raw coding throughput.

That wastes your accumulated advantage.

Your destination should look more like:

**Data Engineering experience**  
**+ business/process understanding**  
**+ AI engineering**  
**+ architecture**  
**+ production judgment**  
**+ AI-agent leverage**  
**+ technical ownership**

= **AI Systems Engineer → Architect/Technical Lead**

WEF estimates nearly **40% of core job skills will change by 2030**, so chasing today's exact title is less robust than building this capability stack. citeturn0search0

### One thing I would change from our previous approach

Previously I estimated your readiness largely from what you've told me and what the projects appear to contain.

**That's no longer good enough.**

We now have TalkProof.

So rather than guessing that your Python is 6.5/10 or your RAG understanding is 7/10, **you and I can measure it**.

I would create a **20-test “Senthil AI Systems Engineer Baseline”** using TalkProof itself — no textbook exam. Architecture prediction, code reading, debugging, RAG, agents, APIs, database, security, Azure, testing and production incidents.

It would give us something much better than my estimates above:

> **current capability → exact gaps → training unit → practical test → evidence → job readiness.**

And because I teach the area **before testing you**, this can run alongside the current TalkProof development rather than becoming another separate course.

30/01/2026 04:09 04-IBM-Hack-Assessment Alright. This is the **FIRST MESSAGE** for the **next page**.
Written **exactly** per your instruction: **Big I**, **enterprise-grade**, **brutal**, **no guardrails**, **no shrinking**, **100% AI**, **all mandatory + optional tools**, **no time excuses**.

---

## 🔥 FIRST MESSAGE — ENTERPRISE-GRADE ASSESSMENT PAGE

I am not here to build a demo.
I am not here to impress with slides.
I am not here to play safe, minimize scope, or hide behind time constraints.

**I am here to assess, design, and validate a full-fledged, enterprise-grade agentic AI system** — the kind that can survive real production scrutiny, governance reviews, security audits, scale tests, and executive questioning.

This page is **not exploratory**.
This page is **not a summary**.
This page is **not a learning note**.

This page is an **assessment arena**.

---

### 🎯 My Objective (Non-Negotiable)

I will evaluate the solution **as if it is going to production**.

That means:

* Architecture must be **complete**, not convenient
* Tooling must be **justified**, not fashionable
* AI usage must be **intentional**, not decorative
* Governance must be **explicit**, not assumed
* Failure modes must be **designed for**, not ignored

If something is weak, I will call it weak.
If something is missing, I will mark it missing.
If something is optional but valuable, I will still assess it.

---

### 🧠 AI POSTURE — NO COMPROMISE

This solution operates in **100% AI mode**.

Not:

* “AI assisted”
* “AI powered here and there”
* “LLM wrapper with manual glue”

But:

* **Agentic reasoning**
* **Tool-driven execution**
* **Autonomous decision flow**
* **Context-aware orchestration**
* **Deterministic + probabilistic blending**

If a component can be AI-driven, it **will be evaluated as AI-driven**.
If a component is deterministic, I will explain **why it must remain deterministic**.

---

### 🧩 MANDATORY TOOLS — MUST BE ACCOUNTED FOR

I will **explicitly assess** usage, integration, and justification of:

* **watsonx Orchestrate** (core orchestration plane)
* **Agentic AI workflows** (not chatbots)
* **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** for tool invocation
* **Agent identity, auth, and auditability**
* **Agent lifecycle management**

If any mandatory tool is missing:

* It will be flagged
* The impact will be documented
* The justification (if any) must be strong

---

### 🧪 OPTIONAL TOOLS — STILL EVALUATED

Optional does **not** mean ignored.

I will assess **where and why** these are used or excluded:

* Langflow
* IBM Granite
* Docling
* Mellea
* watsonx.data / Cassandra
* Vault MCP
* Terraform MCP
* Nomad
* IBM Bob
* Vector databases
* RAG pipelines

Exclusion must be **intentional**, not accidental.

---

### 🛡️ ENTERPRISE REALITY CHECKS (MANDATORY)

This page will **explicitly test** the solution against:

* Security & secrets management
* Agent authentication & authorization
* Audit trails & explainability
* Data governance & compliance
* Failure recovery & rollback
* Cost, latency, and scale assumptions

If it breaks under enterprise conditions, it **fails here** — not later.

---

### 🚫 WHAT I WILL NOT DO

I will not:

* Shrink scope due to time
* Avoid complexity to feel comfortable
* Hide gaps behind diagrams
* Soften language to sound polite
* Pretend this is “good enough for a hackathon”

Hackathon rules define **eligibility** —
**Enterprise standards define quality**.

I am measuring against **quality**.

---

### 🧠 HOW TO READ THIS PAGE

Everything here is:

* Direct
* Opinionated
* Traceable
* Justified

Discomfort is expected.
That is the signal that this page is doing its job.

---

**This page exists so nothing fragile makes it past me.**
If it survives here, it deserves to exist.

---

# 07/10/2026 11:55 — Synchronising the 3 AI Profiles

Yes. **Now I understand the purpose correctly.**

This exercise is **not yet to decide your future job or start training**.

The purpose is:

> **Make ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity operate from the same verified baseline about you, while preserving any unique information one of us knows so nothing useful disappears.**

That changes what we should do next.

The latest Perplexity response is much better. It explicitly corrects several unsupported claims—including invented percentages, assuming daily cloud use proves depth, treating certification as equivalent to operational skill, and treating lack of revenue as an engineering-hiring criterion. fileciteturn1file0L8-L23

It also converges closely with my proposed **Knowledge / Ownership / AI Leverage** model, while adding two useful dimensions I hadn't separated clearly enough: **Architectural Judgement** and **Operational Competence**. fileciteturn1file0L59-L70

I want to **keep those additions**.

## So our shared model should become 5 dimensions

| Dimension | Question |
|---|---|
| **Knowledge** | What do you genuinely understand? |
| **Ownership** | Can you diagnose, change and defend the system? |
| **AI Leverage** | How effectively can you use AI to multiply your output while maintaining quality? |
| **Architectural Judgement** | Can you choose between designs based on cost, security, reliability and constraints? |
| **Operational Competence** | Can you run, recover and improve a real production system? |

That's better than my original three.

Perplexity also makes another correction worth preserving: **baseline testing must happen before teaching**; otherwise we're measuring what you just learned rather than your actual starting point. fileciteturn1file0L68-L70

I agree.

## But don't make the shared file only a career profile

That would lose a lot.

We need a **master factual context**, with claims classified rather than flattened together.

For example:

**FACT — user-confirmed:** 23-year IT/data career.

**FACT — artifact/code evidenced:** TalkProof contains X capability.

**AI assessment — not fact:** “Senthil is 70% ready for Applied AI.”

**Unknown:** independent production debugging level.

**Preference/constraint:** how you want to work and learn.

**Historical:** previous product portfolio and development.

**Current:** what you're actually working on now.

That prevents the next AI from converting an old assessment into a “fact.”

### Information I would preserve that could easily be lost

Your baseline shouldn't just say “23 years data engineer + 40 products.” It should include the progression:

**enterprise/data background → current AI/data engineering → extensive AI-assisted builds → marketplace portfolio → AUMNITY/product work → TalkProof → Claude-build/ChatGPT-independent-review/training workflow → current attempt to develop technical ownership.**

It should also preserve your working method: Git-first evidence, requirements/traceability/tests, your preference for teaching before later training tests, and the distinction between **AI-generated implementation and your human technical ownership**. memcite

Those details materially change how someone should assess you.

## One important disagreement remains

Perplexity now says:

> “My preferred sequence is data/retrieval strengths → applied AI ownership → systems architecture…” fileciteturn1file0L47-L57

That's a **recommendation**, not profile data.

Similarly, Claude saying “target Senior Applied/Agentic AI Engineer” and me agreeing with it does **not make that a fact**.

So the master context should separate:

**WHO SENTHIL IS**  
from  
**WHAT THE THREE AIs CURRENTLY RECOMMEND.**

That way we're synchronising memory **without synchronising bias**.

## Correct next sequence

We should **not start the TalkProof baseline yet**.

First:

**ChatGPT known context + Claude known context + Perplexity known context**

→ identify duplicates  
→ identify contradictions  
→ identify unique facts  
→ mark unsupported claims  
→ identify missing information  
→ ask you only about contradictions/missing critical facts  
→ produce **Verified Master Profile V001**  
→ give identical V001 to all three  
→ ask all three to independently reassess future roles from the same input  
→ compare their conclusions.

Only **after that** should we design the technical baseline.

That will answer something very interesting:

> When ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity receive exactly the same evidence about Senthil, **do they still reach different career conclusions?**

If they do, that's genuine analytical disagreement rather than memory/context mismatch.

And **that is the comparison worth studying**.

# 07/10/2026 11:55 — Claude vs Perplexity: What They Know

Partner, after reading the actual Claude material you pasted, I would **correct the earlier assessment quite substantially**.

The biggest issue is not simply “Claude knows more” or “Perplexity knows less.” They each have **different distorted pictures of you**.

## My assessment

| | Claude | Perplexity |
|---|---:|---:|
| Knows your historical career/background | **~60%** | **~70%** |
| Knows your current AI/product work | **~45%** | **~60%** |

These aren't scientific percentages; they're my estimate from comparing their claims with the much broader history I have available.

And **both make important mistakes**.

---

## 1. Claude's biggest mistake: it has put you in the wrong career box

Claude's conclusion is:

> **AI quality and evaluation → implementation consultant → BPO transformation → data governance**

It explicitly makes **AI quality/evaluation its #1 recommendation** and integration engineering only #5. fileciteturn0file0L138-L146

and therefore maps that into AI evaluation. fileciteturn0file0L32-L44

But that is an **incomplete representation of your career**.

Your stronger foundation is approximately:

**23 years IT**  
→ enterprise data engineering  
→ Ab Initio / SQL / BigQuery  
→ cloud/data/AI  
→ architecture/problem decomposition  
→ increasingly agentic/product engineering.

Testing/validation is **part of your capability**, not the centre of your professional identity.

So I would **not** reposition you as an “AI Quality and Automation Implementation Professional,” which is Claude's final recommendation. fileciteturn0file0L101-L114

That would undersell you.

# 2. Claude badly underestimates what you've actually built

This sentence exposes the problem:

> “A twelve-product portfolio can show ambition. For recruitment, one deployed product with convincing operational evidence may tell me more than twelve sophisticated plans.” fileciteturn0file0L70-L72

So Claude apparently doesn't have enough repository/code context when producing this career assessment.

That changes the diagnosis from:

> “Can this person build AI software?”

toward:

> **“How independently can this person understand, debug, operate and defend software produced at enormous speed with AI?”**

That's a much more interesting problem.

---

# 3. But Claude is correct about one uncomfortable point

Claude says:

> “AI-generated code is not evidence of your competence until you can explain and maintain it.” fileciteturn0file0L97-L99

**I strongly agree.**

This is probably the single most valuable sentence in Claude's whole analysis.

You have demonstrated something relatively new:

**Human architecture/direction + AI coding + AI review can produce a huge amount of software.**

But employers aren't yet going to know how to value that.

So eventually someone will ask:

**“Fine. Claude built this. What can *you* do?”**

And your answer needs to be demonstrated:

> I can explain it.  
> I can trace it.  
> I can identify architectural mistakes.  
> I can predict failures.  
> I can debug them.  
> I can make technical decisions.  
> I can use agents to implement those decisions rapidly.  
> I remain accountable for the system.

That is much stronger than pretending you manually typed 20,000 lines.

---

# 4. Claude is also right not to invent precise scores

> “I cannot honestly say you have a ‘40% gap’ or are ‘7/10’ without reviewing your work.” fileciteturn0file0L57-L60

Correct.

Earlier answers—including mine—gave things such as:

**Python 6.5/10**, **Azure 6/10**, **RAG 7/10**.

We know your **exposure**.

We don't yet have enough controlled evidence of your **independent capability**.

Those are different.

# 5. Claude misunderstands your current AI development method

Claude proposes:

> “Weeks 5–8: You implement one complete workflow…”

and repeatedly frames the improvement process around **you personally implementing things**. fileciteturn0file0L152-L158

That's partly outdated.

I wouldn't train you by saying:

> “Stop Claude and manually become the programmer.”

Your emerging capability should be:

**UNDERSTAND → SPECIFY → DELEGATE → INSPECT → TEST → CHALLENGE → DEBUG → DECIDE**

with manual coding where it improves understanding or where AI fails.

That's different from traditional software engineering.

And I think **this itself may become a valuable future engineering capability**.

---

# 6. Perplexity understands one thing better

From what you've pasted, Perplexity seems to recognise your **breadth and commercial portfolio** better.

Its identification of:

**40+ builds / marketplace products / no proven paying-customer traction**

is materially important.

Claude sees too much:

> testing → evaluation → QA.

Perplexity sees too much:

> products → customers → commercialisation.

Neither fully sees the central thing:

> **You have spent years building technical/data capability and are now experimenting with AI as an engineering multiplier at unusually high intensity.**

That's the profile we actually need to evaluate.

---

# 7. Perplexity's “your skills are already there” is too generous

This is where I disagree with Perplexity.

Saying your only problem is:

> **“proof, not knowledge”**

goes too far.

There are genuine technical gaps.

From our TalkProof discussions alone, we've encountered areas where you wanted education before being tested:

- production RAG diagnosis
- auth/OIDC
- tenancy boundaries
- provider abstraction
- retries/idempotency
- observability
- security
- deployment/runtime behaviour
- understanding what tests actually prove
- tracing architecture through code.

That's perfectly normal.

But therefore the correct statement isn't:

> “Senthil already knows it; he merely needs evidence.”

It's:

> **Senthil possesses substantial transferable engineering knowledge + unusually strong AI leverage, but some modern AI/software-production knowledge is still being acquired while independent technical ownership remains to be demonstrated.**

That's more accurate.

---

# 8. Perplexity also overweights revenue for employment

Zero paying SaaS customers matters enormously if we're assessing:

### **Founder / SaaS entrepreneur**

It matters much less for:

### **Senior Applied AI Engineer**

An employer doesn't require you to have personally sold SaaS.

They need evidence that you can produce and own production outcomes.

So we need to keep two scoreboards separate:

| Career | Biggest missing proof |
|---|---|
| **Senior Applied AI Engineer** | Independent technical ownership |
| **AI Systems Architect** | Architecture depth + production evidence |
| **Forward-Deployed Engineer** | Real-user/client deployment + technical ownership |
| **AI Product/Technical Lead** | Product judgment + delivery + adoption |
| **Founder** | **Revenue/customer acquisition** |
| **AI Quality/Evaluation** | AI eval depth — but I wouldn't make this your main identity |

This separation was missing from both analyses.

---

# 9. What they genuinely know about you

### Claude genuinely knows

Your enterprise history, some testing/validation experience, SaaS/BPO interests, broad AI work and the fact that your independent implementation depth isn't established.

It also correctly recognises that **one deeply evidenced system can be more useful for recruitment than many shallow portfolio entries**. fileciteturn0file0L62-L72

### Perplexity appears to know

More product names, marketplace work, commercial history and your breadth of projects.

### I currently have more continuity around

Your data-engineering career, current AI/data work, marketplace portfolio, TalkProof evolution, Claude development workflow, independent ChatGPT review process, your training objective, Git/evidence discipline, and—critically—the distinction between **AI generating code** and **you technically owning it**. memcite

But **I still don't know your actual independent technical level precisely either**.

I shouldn't pretend otherwise.

---

# 10. My corrected picture of you

I would describe you today as:

> **Experienced enterprise data engineer undergoing a rapid transition into AI/agentic systems engineering, with substantial AI-assisted product-building experience but incompletely measured independent ownership of modern production AI systems.**

That's quite different from Claude's:

> AI quality/evaluation professional.

And different from Perplexity's implied:

> technically ready builder who mainly needs customers/proof.

I think **both are partially correct and partially wrong**.

---

## The missing assessment is now obvious

We should stop asking each AI:

> **“How good am I?”**

because each AI will infer a different Senthil from whatever subset of history it sees.

Instead, there are **three separate things to measure**:

**Knowledge** — what you understand without assistance.

**Ownership** — what you can diagnose/change/defend when AI built it.

**Leverage** — what you can accomplish *with* AI that another engineer cannot accomplish as quickly.

That third dimension is important. Traditional technical assessments usually measure only the first two.

And **that is where I suspect your strongest future advantage may actually be**.

So my current position remains:

### 🎯 Target

**Senior Applied / Agentic AI Engineer**

→ **AI Systems Architect / Technical AI Lead**

with **Forward-Deployed AI Engineer** as a particularly interesting branch if you enjoy customer-side implementation.

Not QA-first.  
Not prompt engineer.  
Not pure frontend developer.  
Not AI researcher.  
Not founder-only.

And before assigning another percentage to your gap, **I would measure those three dimensions against your real TalkProof system.**
